subject: general
question: Which of the following European powers was the first to arrive in India by sea route?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Portuguese**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama** was the first European to reach India via the sea route. He arrived in **Calicut** (now Kozhikode, Kerala) on **May 20, 1498**.
 
• This journey marked the establishment of the **direct sea route between Europe and India**, bypassing traditional overland routes controlled by Middle Eastern traders.
 
• The Portuguese were motivated by trade opportunities, particularly in **spices** like pepper and cardamom, which were highly valued in Europe.
 
• Following Vasco da Gama's success, the Portuguese established several trading posts and settlements along the Indian coastline, including **Goa**, which became their major stronghold in India.
 
• The Portuguese influence in India lasted for centuries, laying the foundation for European colonialism in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **French:**

 
 
• The French arrived in India much later, establishing their first trading post in **Pondicherry** in **1674**.
 
• They had a relatively limited presence in India compared to the Portuguese, Dutch, and English.
 
• The French influence was concentrated in the regions of Pondicherry, Mahe, Karaikal, and Chandernagore.
 
 
 
• **Dutch:**
 
 
• The Dutch East India Company established its presence in India in **1605**, starting with a factory at Masulipatnam.
 
• Their focus was primarily on trade in spices, textiles, and indigo.
 
• Unlike the Portuguese, the Dutch did not seek territorial control but focused on commercial interests.
 
 
 
• **English:**
 
 
• The English East India Company arrived in India in **1608**, starting their first factory at Surat.
 
• Their involvement gradually transitioned from trade to territorial control, eventually leading to the colonization of India.
 
• The English influence became dominant after the decline of other European powers in India.
 
 
 
• **Portuguese Contributions:**
 
 
• The Portuguese introduced several crops to India, including **cashew nuts, potatoes, tomatoes, and tobacco**.
 
• Their architectural legacy is evident in the form of churches and forts, especially in Goa.
 
• They also influenced Indian cuisine, introducing dishes like vindaloo and bebinca.
